title: Application of Neuroscience Tools in Building Construction – An Interdisciplinary Analysis
review_question: To systematically review the interdisciplinary applications of neuroscience tools in building construction, identify the knowledge structure, and highlight key research topics.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Literature from Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed databases using specific neuroscience tool search terms (e.g., ECG, EMG, EDA, ET, EEG, ERP, fNIRS, fMRI, TNS) combined with building/built/construction/architectur/indoor terms. Additional records from article references were included. Exclusions were made for duplicates, topics irrelevant to construction or human psychology/health, non-application of neuroscience tools, non-English documents, and non-article/review document types.

findings.antecedent: Indoor built environment (microclimate: temperature, humidity, light)
findings.consequent: Human physiological and psychological stress response, comfort perception, satisfaction
findings.quote: Indoor built environment generates a microclimate that creates a certain temperature, humidity, light and other conditions, integrating various physical phenomena interacting with the space, while the human body has a dynamically physiological and psychological stress response to changes in the indoor environment, affecting the comfort perception and satisfaction with the indoor environment.

findings.antecedent: High concentrations of indoor air pollution (ozone, carbon dioxide, aerosols, particulate matter)
findings.consequent: Human physiology, neurophysiology, physical and mental health
findings.quote: These tools have also been employed to uncover the effects of high concentrations of ozone, carbon dioxide, aerosols, particulate matter and other air pollution on human physiology, neurophysiology as well as other physical and mental health aspects

findings.antecedent: Different light conditions, light sources, lighting tools
findings.consequent: Human visual comfort, sleep, attention, alertness, mood
findings.quote: Moreover, the tools have been instrumental in identifying the effects of different light conditions, light sources, and lighting tools on human visual comfort, sleep, attention, alertness, and mood, among others

findings.antecedent: Different types and levels of noise
findings.quote: Furthermore, studies have described the use of these tools to successfully identify the effects of different types and levels of noise on human physiological and psychological responses

findings.consequent: Human comfort, mental stress, happiness, physiological and psychological effects
findings.quote: scholars explored the effects of indoor plants on human comfort, mental stress, happiness as well as other physiological and psychological effects
and the effects of different plants and colors in outdoor green spaces and the layout of green landscape on mental health

findings.antecedent: Neuroscience tools (vs. traditional safety assessment methods like interviews/questionnaires)
findings.quote: In recent years, neuroscience tools have been gradually applied as a more immediate and objective method.

findings.antecedent: EEG (measurement of physical and mental fatigue)
findings.consequent: Construction workers' safety hazards (trips, falls, impacts), workers' mental and emotional state (depression, stress), health, productivity
findings.quote: EEG can be applied to measure the level of physical and mental fatigue among construction workers and assess the safety hazards, such as trips, falls, and impacts, caused by workers' mental and emotional state including depression, and stress, thereby improving health and productivity

findings.antecedent: Eye tracking (exploration of visual search and attention allocation patterns of workers with different personality traits, knowledge levels, experience)
findings.consequent: Identification of on-site hazards, analysis of hazard probability (caused by search defects)
findings.quote: Scholars have also employed eye tracking to explore the visual search and attention allocation patterns of workers with different personality traits, knowledge levels, and experience levels... This approach has enabled effectively identification of on-site hazards, and analysis of the probability of hazards caused by search defects

findings.consequent: Workers' attitudes/willingness to train safely, degree of improvement in safety hazard recognition ability (under different training modes), post-training safety warning, job performance assessment systems
findings.quote: Neuroscience tools, targeting neuroscience measurement, are also commonly used to study workers' attitudes and willingness to train safely, assess the degree of improvement in safety hazard recognition ability under different training modes, and establish post-training safety warning as well as job performance assessment systems

findings.consequent: Aesthetic effect of architectural elements, relationship between observer's gaze pattern and formal properties (architectural elements under different design parameters)
findings.quote: architects usually use eye tracking technology to not only determine the aesthetic effect of architectural elements but also explore the relationship between the observer's gaze pattern with the formal properties of architectural elements under different design parameters

findings.consequent: Key psychological dimensions (sensitive to specific design parameters), neural features evoked
findings.quote: Previous studies have also reported the use of ERP and fMRI in analysis of key psychological dimensions sensitive to specific design parameters and the neural features evoked

findings.antecedent: Combination of virtual reality (VR) with EEG/ERP, ET
findings.consequent: Neurophysiological information (human subjective feelings, cognitive functions) across different interior environments (proportion of functional areas, lighting designs, room color schemes, furniture color, spatial environment designs), human emotions, security, comfort
findings.quote: For interior environment design, a combination of virtual reality (VR) with EEG/ERP, ET has been used to effectively measure neurophysiological information related to human subjective feelings as well as cognitive functions across different interior environments. These include the proportion of interior functional areas, lighting designs, room color schemes, furniture color and other spatial environment designs, with respect to human emotions, security and comfort

findings.antecedent: High-resolution, immersive virtual reality (VR) technology, in combination with EEG and ET
findings.consequent: Human way finding data (working memory, cognitive workload) during navigation tasks (different route parameters), optimal route plan for interior design
findings.quote: In terms of navigation design, since indoor wayfinding is a daily and complex activity, current researches have also applied high-resolution, immersive virtual reality (VR) technology, in combination with EEG and ET, to mine human way finding data. Consequently, these data have enabled effective understanding of the working memory and cognitive workload during execution of navigation tasks by designing different route parameters in the virtual platform, and finally propose the optimal route plan for interior design

findings.consequent: Occupational health hazards (construction workers), degree of chronic muscle fatigue, musculoskeletal disorders
findings.quote: Current EMG techniques in neuroscience have been applied in analysis of occupational health hazards among construction workers, such as in identification of the degree of chronic muscle fatigue, an important cause of musculoskeletal disorders

findings.antecedent: Continuous monitoring of biomechanical variables (trunk muscle activity, trunk kinematics) through surface electromyography and motion sensing
findings.consequent: Tasks causing excessive physical strain on construction workers
findings.quote: Particularly, this has been achieved by continuously monitoring biomechanical variables, including trunk muscle activity and trunk kinematics through surface electromyography and motion sensing... thereby determining which tasks cause excessive physical strain on construction workers.
HRV level is considered to be an indicator of physiological stress or arousal, increasing with low HRV
HRV level is considered to be an indicator of physiological stress or arousal... decreasing with high HRV.
research has revealed that cold indoor temperatures have a negative effect on cardiovascular health
HRV is sensitive to changes in ambient temperature and human thermal sensation and may be utilized as a potential physiological indicator of human thermal comfort

findings.consequent: Sympathetic nerves (more active state), emotions (stress, anxiety)
findings.quote: When thermal sensation is significant or thermal discomfort is present, sympathetic nerves are in a more active state and can trigger emotions such as stress and anxiety

findings.antecedent: Higher levels of indoor exposure to carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, ozone
findings.consequent: HRV (elevated), parasympathetic regulation (decreased RMSSD, HF, pNN50), sympathetic drive (increased SDNN, LF, LF/HF)
findings.quote: studies have demonstrated that higher levels of indoor exposure to carbon monoxide... carbon dioxide... and ozone... result in elevated HRV, as reflected by decreased parasympathetic regulation (RMSSD, HF, pNN50) and increased sympathetic drive (SDNN, LF, LF/HF)

findings.antecedent: Increased exposure to indoor particle pollutants (PM2.5)
findings.quote: while increased exposure to indoor particle pollutants, especially PM2.5, causes HRV levels to decrease... thus increasing cardiovascular risk

findings.antecedent: LF/HF ratio of viewing plants (different colors)
findings.quote: it is demonstrated that the LF/HF ratio of viewing plants of different colors is significantly negatively correlated to human satisfaction
the amplitude of the EMG increases with the degree of fatigue during the process of muscle isometric contraction to fatigue
the EMG activity of lumbar muscles decreases significantly when bending over to assemble rebar
the use of passive exoskeleton systems significantly reduces lumbar vertical spine muscle activity

findings.antecedent: Weight lifting loads (with passive exoskeleton systems)
findings.consequent: Lumbar vertical spine muscle activity reduction
findings.quote: the reduction is even greater when weight lifting loads

findings.antecedent: Female house painters (performing identical work tasks)
findings.quote: female house painter have a higher relative muscle load than their male counterparts

findings.antecedent: Excessively high or excessively low indoor temperature
findings.quote: excessively high or excessively low indoor temperature... can increase EDA, thereby increasing work stress for indoor workers.
a cold white lighting environment... can increase EDA, thereby increasing work stress for indoor workers.

findings.antecedent: Prolonged period in a noisy environment
findings.quote: When people spend an extended period in a noisy environment, their respiration rate drops sharply and their EDA levels significantly increase

findings.antecedent: Indoor placement of plants and artificial windows
findings.quote: Indoor placement of plants and artificial windows reduces people's SCL levels, demonstrating that natural elements can be effective in relieving stress and reducing arousal
similarly installing green walls indoors helps alleviate negative emotions
studies have found that workers with loads produce higher EDA values than those without loads
SCR may be used to measure and quantify the effect of geometric manipulation of building spaces on human emotional responses

findings.antecedent: Irregular exterior window shapes and sunlight exposure conditions
findings.quote: as well as the effect of irregular exterior window shapes and sunlight exposure conditions on occupant pleasantness in the interior
glare is a significant factor affecting the visual comfort of indoor personnel.
PUI, BA, FR, and other indicators can indicate visual discomfort caused by glare
increasing ambient luminance contrast can improve efficiency in a non-glare environment

findings.antecedent: Visual search patterns of workers (correctly identify hazards vs. not)
findings.quote: the visual search patterns of workers who correctly identify hazards differ from those who do not

findings.consequent: Workers' decreased ability to detect hazards
findings.quote: attention deficit and mental fatigue being the primary reasons for workers' decreased ability to detect hazards.
the use of wearable eye-tracking equipment can help identify construction hazards more accurately.

findings.antecedent: Scan paths and fixation heat maps (generated by ET technology)
findings.consequent: Focused or personalized feedback to workers, hazard recognition
findings.quote: scan paths and fixation heat maps generated by ET technology can effectively reveal focused or personalized feedback to workers, and this feedback communicates to workers defects in the search process, eliciting reflection and thereby facilitating hazard recognition

biophilic design elements such as greenery are gaining popularity, and the use of eye movement metrics such as total fixation time can help designers better understand how office design can contribute to occupant's health and performance

findings.consequent: Brain rhythms, power spectral densities (PSD) of brain electricity, thermal comfort, thermal pleasure
findings.quote: of the indoor thermal environment, and temperature changes affect brain rhythms and the power spectral densities (PSD) of brain electricity, which affects thermal comfort and thermal pleasure.

findings.antecedent: Construction noise, prolonged indoor noise (building sound environment)
findings.quote: Construction noise, as well as prolonged indoor noise in the building sound environment, can affect people's minds and bodies.

findings.antecedent: Varying degrees of illumination and color temperatures (lighting environment)
findings.consequent: Alpha band (brain activity), people's mental states
findings.quote: The alpha band which is excited by varying degrees of illumination and color temperatures in the lighting environment can reflect people's mental states.

findings.antecedent: Poor indoor air quality, high pollution levels
findings.consequent: Theta and beta powers of human brain (increase), bad moods
findings.quote: When indoor air quality is poor and pollution levels are high, theta and beta powers of the human brain increase and can result in bad moods

findings.consequent: Alpha waves of human brain (more active), personal stress
findings.quote: the alpha waves of the human brain are more active when viewing indoor plants and can significantly relieve personal stress.

findings.consequent: Different brain wave patterns, emotional state, attention level, mental workload
findings.quote: When workers are subjected to different stressors during construction, different brain wave patterns are generated, reflecting their emotional state, attention level, mental workload, and other mental activities.

findings.antecedent: Monitoring and identification of worker fatigue (using EEG)
findings.quote: Monitoring and identification of worker fatigue using EEG can significantly reduce construction hazards
low-frequency gamma waves can also reflect workers' vigilance and attention levels.
theta waves in the anterior cingulate cortex are associated with the emotional perception of specific geometric landscapes.

findings.consequent: Architectural design, environments meeting human needs (understanding impact of design on human perception/experience)
findings.quote: EEG can help improve the architectural design and create environments that meet human needs by better understanding the impact of architectural design on human perception and subjective experience.
Scholars have discovered that the prefrontal and hippocampal brain areas are involved in the evaluation of architectural aesthetics

findings.consequent: Activation of the parahippocampus place area, perceived beauty
findings.quote: the primary factor affecting the activation of the parahippocampus place area being the openness of the space, which is typically regarded as more beautiful

findings.consequent: Aesthetic judgments (architectural design), visuospatial processing (activates left anterior cuneiform and left middle frontal gyrus)
findings.quote: By studying the effect of ceiling height on aesthetic judgments in architectural design, researchers discovered that visuospatial processing activates the left anterior cuneiform and left middle frontal gyrus of the brain

findings.antecedent: Certain contemplative buildings (e.g., museums, churches, libraries)
findings.consequent: Contemplative states, significant activation of the left posterior central gyrus and left inferior parietal phase
findings.quote: Specific architectural styles can also induce contemplative states; for example, certain contemplative buildings... cause significant activation of the left posterior central gyrus and left inferior parietal phase, eliciting contemplative experiences

findings.consequent: Limbic gyrus (cingulate, parahippocampal), adhesion locations (anterior cuneus, posterior lobe of the cerebellum)
findings.quote: it was discovered that persistent noise exposure may alter the limbic gyrus (particularly the cingulate and parahippocampal gyrus), as well as adhesion locations, including the anterior cuneus and posterior lobe of the cerebellum

findings.antecedent: fNIRS recordings of workers' prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity
findings.quote: fNIRS recordings of workers' prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity reveal a negative association between PFC activity and hazard recognition ability

findings.consequent: Different cortical regions of the PFC (left PFC, dorsolateral PFC, ventral PFC)
findings.quote: During hazard recognition, different cortical regions of the PFC are differentially and continuously activated, with the left PFC being more involved, the dorsolateral PFC is used for electrical and shock-related hazard recognition, and the ventral PFC being used for stab-related hazard recognition

findings.antecedent: Fall hazards (vs. electrical and fire hazards)
findings.quote: when compared to other hazards such as electrical and fire hazards, fall hazards activate the brain more and use significant cognitive resources

findings.consequent: Workers' ability to identify hazards (HRA index)
findings.quote: some researchers have also developed an HRA index to measure workers' ability to identify hazards using PFC activation data obtained via fNIRS

findings.antecedent: fNIRs (monitoring and classifying real-time cognitive load)
findings.quote: fNIRs are being employed in indoor wayfinding research, where they are used to assist in the design of adaptive wayfinding systems by monitoring and classifying real-time cognitive load

synthesis_conclusions: Neuroscience tools have expanded beyond medical and psychological applications to humanities, social sciences, engineering, and other disciplines, leading to cross-fertilization of interdisciplinary knowledge.
The discipline of building construction is a perfect example of the interdisciplinary application of neuroscience tools, significantly aiding research to improve building safety, comfort, and health.

ET and EEG are the most frequently used neuroscience tools in building construction research, primarily due to their ability to discover visual search patterns and monitor mental/cognitive status in real-time, and their suitability for non-laboratory research via wearable sensing devices.
China and the United States demonstrate the strongest research capacities in this interdisciplinary field, with their institutions and scholars setting future development trends.

Research on the application of neuroscience tools in building construction is mainly clustered into four directions: built environment, construction safety, architectural design, and occupational health.
ECG is mainly used to study the built environment; EMG for occupational health; fMRI for architectural design; and TNS is at an initial stage with only one article on construction safety.

EDA, ET, EEG, and fNIRs are used across built environment, construction safety, and architectural design, with ET and EEG being the most common for topics like thermal/acoustic/light/air quality, hazard recognition, mental fatigue, safety training, attention/alertness, aesthetic design, spatial design, and biophilic design.
evidence_gaps: Future research should thoroughly investigate the application of neuroscience tools in civil engineering (e.g., bridges, roads, subways), which was excluded from this review.
Future research should utilize co-citation analysis and main path analysis to uncover highly cited literature and citation relationships within this interdisciplinary field.
limitations: This review focuses exclusively on the application of neuroscience tools in building construction, excluding civil engineering applications (e.g., bridges, roads, subways).

Only co-word analysis was used to investigate the application of neuroscience tools, without employing co-citation analysis or main path analysis to identify highly cited literature and citation relationships.

paper_metadata.title: Application of Neuroscience Tools in Building Construction – An Interdisciplinary Analysis
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Application of Neuroscience Tools in Building Construction – An Interdisciplinary Analysis
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Interdisciplinary integration is a new driving force in development of science and technology. Neuroscience, a powerful tool for studying human physiology and psychology that is greatly interconnected with the field of building construction, has attracted numerous research attention. In this paper, we systematically review the interdisciplinary applications of neuroscience tools using bibliometric methods. We report that the built environment, construction safety, architectural design, and occupational health are the main areas of research attention, while thermal comfort, air quality, hazard recognition, safety training, aesthetic design, and biophilic design, among others, comprise the most frequently studied topics with regards to application of neuroscience tools. Currently, eye tracking and the electroencephalogram are the most commonly used tools in the field of building construction, while functional near-infrared spectroscopy, functional magnetic resonance imaging and trigeminal nerve stimulation are still at their initial stage of application.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Natural and restorative environments can restore directed attention and reduce mental fatigue.
Humans have an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems, influencing well-being in built environments.
Exposure to natural environments can lead to physiological and psychological stress reduction.

mechanism_chain.description: Mechanism describing how light in the built environment influences human circadian rhythms and subsequent cognitive and affective states.

steps.from_construct: Light exposure (e.g., specific spectrum, intensity, timing)
steps.to_construct: Activation of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)
Signal transmission to the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN)
Regulation of melatonin secretion from the pineal gland
Entrainment of circadian rhythms and sleep-wake cycles
Impact on cognitive performance, mood, and overall well-being

instruments_used.name: EEG (Electroencephalography)
instruments_used.construct: Brain electrical activity, cognitive load, attention, emotional response
instruments_used.description: Measures electrical activity in the brain via electrodes placed on the scalp to assess neural responses.

instruments_used.name: fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging)
instruments_used.construct: Brain activity, neural correlates of perception, emotion, cognition
instruments_used.description: Detects changes in blood flow to measure brain activity and localize neural responses to environmental stimuli.

instruments_used.name: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
instruments_used.construct: Autonomic nervous system activity, stress, emotional regulation
instruments_used.description: Measures variations in the time interval between heartbeats to assess physiological stress and relaxation.

instruments_used.name: Electrodermal Activity (EDA) / Skin Conductance Response (SCR)
instruments_used.description: Measures changes in the electrical conductivity of the skin, reflecting sympathetic nervous system activity and arousal.

instruments_used.name: Self-report questionnaires (e.g., PANAS, PSS, comfort scales)
instruments_used.construct: Subjective mood, perceived stress, comfort, satisfaction
instruments_used.description: Standardized questionnaires used to capture individuals' subjective experiences and perceptions.
